subject: BridgeWork / Redwood — territory claim handshake & pipeline map
messages:
From: Cassandra Lee <cassandra@orbitops.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Wu <sam.wu@bridgework.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: BridgeWork + Redwood: territory map and co-sell handshake

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the intro last week. Sam and I pulled together the list of accounts where we currently see overlap on active opportunities (attached: initial_account_list.csv). A few notes up front:
- Acme Inc and HelixHealth have parallel POCs active this quarter.
- Neosys is evaluating both our integrations and a partner-led integration that BridgeWork owns.

We want to avoid duplicate outbound and speed up a joint GTM for the largest opportunities. Can we get a simple ownership handshake for pipeline staging + a quick mutual action plan? Specifically:
1) Which of the accounts in the attachment should be partner-owned vs Redwood-owned for outreach?
2) For deals > $500k, what is the escalation path if there’s a territory disagreement?
3) Can we schedule a 30-min sync this week to lock the map and agree on single owner per account?

Attaching a rough CSV of accounts (no-opportunity details). If you want, Sam can share a short deck of how BridgeWork supports co-sell.

Best,
Cassandra Lee
Head of Alliances, OrbitOps
[attachment: initial_account_list.csv (csv)]

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Cassandra Lee <cassandra@orbitops.com>, Sam Wu <sam.wu@bridgework.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeWork + Redwood: territory map and co-sell handshake

Cassandra / Sam — thanks for sending this over and for flagging the high-priority accounts. I’ve attached a first-pass pipeline map (pipeline_map_v2.pdf) that combines our CRM views and the CSV you sent.

Proposed quick rules to avoid duplicate outreach (we can refine):
- Ownership precedence: Partner-owned integrations (partner provides integration and owns technical pre-sales) = partner owns outreach and lead-to-opportunity conversion.
- Redwood-led POC or product-led demo = Redwood owns primary outreach and SDR qualification.
- If both parties are actively running a POC simultaneously, the party with the signed MOU or earliest demo date keeps ownership; the other party will be marked as "supporting co-sell".
- For deals > $500k, we escalate to Sales Ops + Alliances leadership for a tie-breaker (aim <48 hours).

Next steps I propose:
1) We each flag the accounts in the attached map we believe we should own and return with rationale by EOD tomorrow.
2) Schedule a co-sell kickoff (30m) with Sales Ops and your AE to lock ownership for open opportunities.
3) Draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) and baseline SLAs for single-owner outreach cadence.

I attached the consolidated map for your review. Happy to run the kickoff — propose Wed 10am PT or Thu 2pm PT.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Partner Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
[attachment: pipeline_map_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Cassandra Lee <cassandra@orbitops.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Sam Wu <sam.wu@bridgework.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeWork + Redwood: territory map and co-sell handshake

On Mon, Apr 12, 2027 at 9:03 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> Cassandra / Sam — thanks for sending this over and for flagging the high-priority accounts. I’ve attached a first-pass pipeline map (pipeline_map_v2.pdf) that combines our CRM views and the CSV you sent.
> 
> Proposed quick rules to avoid duplicate outreach (we can refine): ...

Thanks Dylan — the rules look reasonable. Two clarifications:
- Escalation timing: can we shorten tie-breaker window to 24 hours for strategic accounts (Acme, HelixHealth)? Those deals have active exec attention.
- For larger deals we also need a simple credit/split rule if both parties generate pipeline (example: 70/30 revenue credit to the owner unless otherwise negotiated).

Attached is a short scan of BridgeWork’s partner agreement template for your legal team to eyeball (MWP_contract_scan.pdf). Sam and I can join the kickoff at either Wed 10am PT or Thu 2pm PT — Wed works best for us.

Appreciate it,
Cassandra
Head of Alliances, OrbitOps
[attachment: MWP_contract_scan.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeWork + Redwood: territory map and co-sell handshake

Looping you both in — quick note from GTM leadership perspective:
- We should avoid creating per-partner special rules for every account. Keep the matrix simple and deterministic (owner by integration/POC status + signed MOU).
- Sales Ops should enforce ownership flags in CRM and block duplicate sequence sends when an account is assigned.
- For strategic customers (Acme, HelixHealth), escalate directly to Sales Dir + Alliances Dir <24h as Cassandra requested.

If Sales Ops needs an artifact, I have a short policy doc we can repurpose. Happy to run the kickoff and align exec touches.

-Marissa
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeWork + Redwood: territory map and co-sell handshake

Agree with Marissa. Proposed ownership matrix (short):
- Integration owner = partner (if partner delivers integration & main technical contact)
- Product/feature POC = Redwood owner (we control product roadmap/demos)
- Joint solution (both build) = joint ownership; default outreach owner = the party that generated the first qualified opportunity in CRM (timestamp wins).
- Revenue credit: default to owner unless partner provides signed BOM or lead-conversion evidence; any splits must be agreed in writing before close.

I uploaded a one-pager to Drive with an example workflow and the tie-breaker process: https://drive.redwood.com/s/BridgeWork-PipelineMap-v2

If everyone is good with the matrix, we should publish it as the canonical policy and have Sales Ops implement flags and automated sequence suppression.

-Karthik
Sr. Manager, Alliances Operations

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Cassandra Lee <cassandra@orbitops.com>, Sam Wu <sam.wu@bridgework.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeWork + Redwood: territory map and co-sell handshake

Cassandra / Sam — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the contract scan.

Summary and next steps:
- We’ll adopt the ownership matrix Karthik outlined as the default policy.
- For Acme and HelixHealth, we’ll use the accelerated 24h escalation path.
- I’ve attached a starter mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.xlsx) — please review and suggest edits.
- Let’s lock the co-sell kickoff: Wed 14 Apr 2027, 10:00am PT. I’ll send the calendar invite and include Sales Ops + your AE.
- DocuSign: I’ll send a brief MOU template via DocuSign after we agree the MAP edits (link to packet: https://www.docusign.com/packet/RW-MAP-12345).

Appreciate the partnership — excited to get this cleaned up so both teams can move faster.

See you Wed,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Partner Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
